content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will be officially released to all users on Monday, September 14.

At the same time, the company stated that two features originally in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be introduced in a 'future software update' for iPhone: the suggested features in Messages, and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated their website this week to reflect the temporary removal of these two features from iOS 27. The changes also apply to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had previously noticed that iOS 27 beta 5 had already removed the automatic password changing feature, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm the change.

As a reminder, the suggested features in the Messages app provide options to add items to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with a single tap, based on the content of the user's conversations.

Here is Apple's description of the password feature:

The Passwords app will attempt to go directly to websites where your passwords are weak or have been compromised, and automatically update the password. At WWDC, Apple mentioned that this feature would use Apple Intelligence and Safari to 'proactively take action on your behalf'.

As for when these two features will return in iOS 27, there are no further details for now. Apple's website simply states that they will be available in a 'future software update'.
